**Finding: MISSING** (INSURANCE — vendor insurance)

**What I checked**
- Full-text search for "insurance" — zero hits across the entire agreement.
- Section outline — no insurance heading.
- Section 12 (which carries the miscellaneous provisions through Section 30, Force Majeure) — indemnity, liability cap, term, assignment, notices, governing law, etc., but no coverage requirement.

**Why it matters here**
TrueLink is a hosting vendor: it hosts Client's Web Site, holds Client Content, and transmits data through the Interface under System and Credit Repository Agreements. That places it squarely in the rule's walk-away territory — no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data. Neither the preferred position nor the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) appears anywhere, so this is a genuine gap rather than a sub-element shortfall.

Worth noting: the absence is compounded by Section 12's liability cap (p0077), which limits TrueLink's exposure on Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 to 12 months' hosting and support fees. With no insurance backstop, our recovery against TrueLink is thin. I have not flagged the cap itself under this rule — that is a separate liability-rule question.

**Redline proposed** (validated ok:true)
New Section 31 inserted after p0097 at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M covering the hosting and handling of Client Content and other Client data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request; maintained through the term and one year after.

The one-year tail matters given the auto-renewing one-year term and the wind-down periods in Section 13 (30 days for name server, 60 days for hosting environment) — claims can surface after termination. The comment offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M, cyber USD 2M) as a landing zone if TrueLink pushes back on quantum.

Confidence 0.9. The small residual: Section 24's survival clause refers to "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so a new Section 31 sits outside that enumeration. If you want the insurance obligation to survive expressly, the survival list should be conformed to "5 through 31" — a clean-up I'd raise with the numbering rather than under this rule.
